out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Approved Record Keeping, Tags/Labels
violations.observation: A record keeping system is not in place to maintain the tags of used/sold shellstock in chronological order correlated to the date that is recorded on the tag/label. PIC COULD NOT PROVIDE THE SHELL-STOCK TAGS FOR THE MUSSELS SOLD IN THE PAST 90 DAYS.
violations.corrective_action: Tags/labels must be maintained in chronological order by the date recorded on the tag/label when the last shellstock is used/sold. CDI: PIC RE-EDUCATED ON KEEPING TAGS. ENSURE SHELL-STOCK TAGS ARE KEPT IN CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER FOR 90 DAYS.

violations.title: Shellstock Removed from Tagged or Labeled Container
violations.observation: Shellstock has been removed from the tagged/labeled container without preserving source identification. Observed no shell stock tag with individually packaged raw clams located in the deep freezer.
violations.corrective_action: Shellstock that has been removed from the tagged/labeled container must have a system used to identify source. CDI: PIC RE-EDUCATED. CLAM LABEL RELOCATE TO THE FREEZER WITH THE FROZEN CLAMS.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: RAW HARD SHELL EGGS OVER PRODUCE IN THE TWO DOOR COOLER AND RAW BEEF AND RAW BEEF INTESTINES OVER POTATOES AND ONIONS STORED ON SHELVES IN DRY STORAGE.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CDI: FOODS WERE RE-LOCATED. PIC RE-EDUCATED ON STORING ACCORDING TO COOKING TEMPERATURE. INES PLACE RESTAURANT (Inspection Date: 09/24/2026) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Proper hot holding temperatures

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cooked beans 80F (1HR) located on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. CDI: BEANS WERE MOVED TO STOVE TO REHEAT TO 165F.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) two containers of homemade pickled cabbage (66 F) and box of raw hard shell eggs (66 F) in the back room. All foods were kept out over night. 2) cooked chicken (44F). The foods were out for 1 hour. 3) on dry storage shelving: raw beef at 46f (1hr)
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: 1) FOODS WERE DISCARDED. 2) FOODS WERE PUT IN THE REACH IN COOLER FOR QUICK CHILL. 3) ITEMS WERE PLACED IN COOLER FOR QUICK CHILL.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food, Disclosure
violations.observation: The following raw and/or undercooked foods are provided on the menu, menu board, table tent or brochure without proper disclosure: the consumer advisory disclosure on the menu is not complete.
violations.corrective_action: The Consumer Advisory shall include a disclosure statement that includes a description of the animal-derived foods as raw/undercooked or identification of the animal-derived foods by asterisking (*) them to a footnote that states that the items are served raw or undercooked, or contain raw or undercooked ingredients. ADD “*THIS ITEM MAY CONTAIN UNDERCOOKED OR RAW INGREDIENTS.” IN THE CONSUMER ADVISORY STATEMENT BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION IN 10 DAYS.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Poison/Toxic Material, Conditions of Use
violations.observation: Pesticides labeled for residential use were observed in the facility and are being applied by the operator to control pests. OBSERVED RESIDENTIAL PESTICIDE SPRAY IN THE WATER HEATER ROOM.
violations.corrective_action: Remove residential use pesticides from the facility. When necessary for pest control, chemical pesticides must be applied by a certified pesticide applicator to prevent injury and contamination. CDI: RESIDENTIAL PESTICIDE SPRAY DISPOSED OF DURING INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Food Thermometers, Provided & Accessible
violations.observation: The certified food manager could not provide a food temperature measuring device.
violations.corrective_action: A metal-stemmed probe food thermometer shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures. OBTAIN A THIN PROBE FOOD THERMOMETER BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION IN 10 DAYS.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Controlling Pests, Pest Control Methods
violations.observation: Methods are not being used to control pests. OBSERVED A LIVE COCKROACH IN THE BACK ROOM AND SEVERAL DEAD COCKROACHES IN THE LOBBY. OBSERVED MOUSE DROPPINGS ON THE FLOOR AROUND THE UNSEALED BACK STORAGE ROOM.
violations.corrective_action: Insects and other pests are capable of transmitting disease to people by contaminating food and food-contact surfaces. If pests are found on the premises methods shall be used to control their presence. GET A PEST CONTROL SERVICE FROM LICENSED PEST CONTROL COMPANY WITHIN TEN DAYS FOR RODENTS AND COCKROACHES. FOLLOW ALL RECOMMENDATIONS THE COMPANY GIVES YOU. IN ADDITION, INCREASE THE FREQUENCY OF TREATMENTS TO ENSURE YOU ARE TARGETING COCKROACHES AT EACH LIFE STAGE.

violations.title: Openings Protected from Pest Entry
violations.observation: Openings to the exterior of the building are present along the back door.
violations.corrective_action: Fill or close holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. ENSURE THERE ARE NO OPENINGS AT THE BACK DOOR BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION IN 10 DAYS.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Observed boxed alcohol and cooking oil stored on the floor in the back room.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. ENSURE ALL FOODS ARE STORED 6 INCHES ABOVE THE FLOOR BY YOUR NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: OBSERVED CLEAN CUTTING BOARDS AND KNIVES WERE STORED DIRECTLY ON THE UNSEALED FLOOR OF THE BACK STORAGE ROOM.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. CDI: ITEMS WERE TAKEN TO THE THREE-VAT SINK TO WASH, RINSE, AND SANITIZE. PIC RE-EDUCATED.

out_items.name: Approved thawing methods used

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: fish being thawed on the counter without using running water
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. PIC put the thawing fish under running water

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: pupusa filling being kept out on the counter using time as a public health control did not have time marking
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. Person in charge made time labels for food being kept out on the counter using time as a public health control did

violations.title: Time as a Public Health Control, Written Procedures
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide written procedures for the use of time as a public health control with the following time/temperature control for safety food item(s): facility id don’t have a written procedure pupusa fillings being kept on the counter using time as public health control
violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. Person in charge and EHS established written procedure for using time as a public health control, will follow up in 10 days to verify compliance with written procedures INES PLACE RESTAURANT (Inspection Date: 10/06/2025) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: OBSERVED FULL CONTAINERS OF PREPARED FOODS IN DUKERS 2 DR UR RANGING IN TEMPERATURE OF 45-48F.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. WITH NO WIC, PREPARED FOODS SHOULD BE PORTIONED INTO SMALLER CONTAINERS TO FACILITATE FASTER COOLING TO 41F. INES PLACE RESTAURANT (Inspection Date: 10/24/2024) Page 2 of 3
